There's a difference between moderation and censorship. There is nothing wrong with establishing a few clear rules and enforcing them fairly and transparently.

There's currently a crazed troll over on /v/news posting dozens of links each day, with topics such as 'proof the white race is going extinct' and so on. They can't just ignore that stuff or expect the down vote mechanism to handle it. (Besides, what good is a news forum if you can't sort by 'new'?) It doesn't take long before people start to leave and the subverse just dies.

The folks over at /v/guns are one example of how to do it right. Have a look at the their sidebar to see their forum rules, which are fair and helpful. I'm not suggesting that all of their rules would be suitable here, but it's an example of how to set reasonable and enforceable limits that everyone can be cool with.

The downvote mechanism alone is inadequate for this. It forces everyone to sort by popularity, meaning the new content is buried and everything starts to seem old and stale.

The best forums are moderated with a few, clear rules, that are fairly applied with a transparent process. We have the tools to do that here, with the wonderful "Submissions we removed" and "Comments we removed" links that voat provides. Put those in the sidebar too, so let everyone can see what's going on.

https://voat.co/v/news/modlog/deleted
Unless it's blatantly illegal, that's what the downvote button is for.

I think having it clearly laid out in the rules for the sub is the way to go -- it's up to the mods to decide on where to draw the line, but I think there are conscientious ways of sharing a site or product that doesn't detract from the quality of the sub.

anonomale brings up a good point here; where should we draw the line between spam and sales? At times, I have found useful coupon codes for clothing retail that have been posted by employees of companies on various blog sites. That being said, in my opinion, repeated posting of their branded items without any substance or contribution (especially trying to link directly to the site for traffic) should be removed.

In my personal opinion, and in the spirit of Voat, I say just let them post. If it's a shitpost or an obvious sales pitch, I have faith in the (surprisingly large) community here to downgoat it if it sucks.

If someone posts what is obviously an advertisement for a particular brand or product, it will be upvoated if it's awesome, and I'm ok with that. This of course opens the door for upgoat brigades or voat manipulation, and if we have any evidence of that it should be deleted.
